properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.1
properties.ruleText: RMS return merchandise authorization creation rules
properties.ruleHTML: RMS return merchandise authorization creation rules

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.1.1
properties.ruleText: If a product was purchased more than 30 days ago, then an return merchandise authorization cannot be initiated unless an extended return period applies
properties.ruleHTML: If a product was purchased more than 30 days ago, then an return merchandise authorization cannot be initiated unless an extended return period applies

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.1.2
properties.ruleText: If an return merchandise authorization is being created, then it must be linked to an existing Order ID
properties.ruleHTML: If an return merchandise authorization is being created, then it must be linked to an existing Order ID

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.1.3
properties.ruleText: If a product already has an active return merchandise authorization, then no additional return merchandise authorization can be created for that product until the existing RMA is resolved
properties.ruleHTML: If a product already has an active return merchandise authorization, then no additional return merchandise authorization can be created for that product until the existing RMA is resolved

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.2
properties.ruleText: RMS return merchandise authorization approval rules
properties.ruleHTML: RMS return merchandise authorization approval rules

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.2.1
properties.ruleText: If an return merchandise authorization is requested, then it must be reviewed and approved by a return specialist before the customer is allowed to return the product
properties.ruleHTML: If an return merchandise authorization is requested, then it must be reviewed and approved by a return specialist before the customer is allowed to return the product

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.2.2
properties.ruleText: If an return merchandise authorization is requested, then it must be approved or rejected within 48 hours
properties.ruleHTML: If an return merchandise authorization is requested, then it must be approved or rejected within 48 hours

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.2.3
properties.ruleText: If the return reason is "Defective" or "Damaged in Transit," then the return merchandise authorization must include an inspection upon receipt
properties.ruleHTML: If the return reason is "Defective" or "Damaged in Transit," then the return merchandise authorization must include an inspection upon receipt

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.3
properties.ruleText: RMS product return rules
properties.ruleHTML: RMS product return rules

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.3.1
properties.ruleText: If an return merchandise authorization is approved, then the product must be returned within 14 days; otherwise, the RMA will be automatically canceled.
properties.ruleHTML: If an return merchandise authorization is approved, then the product must be returned within 14 days; otherwise, the RMA will be automatically canceled.

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.3.2
properties.ruleText: If a product is returned, then it must be shipped using a pre-approved carrier with tracking.
properties.ruleHTML: If a product is returned, then it must be shipped using a pre-approved carrier with tracking.

properties.name: RMS RMA Business Rules.3.3
properties.ruleText: If a product is returned without an approved return merchandise authorization or outside the specified return period, then the return will be rejected and the product will be sent back to the customer at their expense.
properties.ruleHTML: If a product is returned without an approved return merchandise authorization or outside the specified return period, then the return will be rejected and the product will be sent back to the customer at their expense.

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm
Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.1
properties.ruleText: robotic picker stop and recalculate path rules
properties.ruleHTML: robotic picker stop and recalculate path rules

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.1.1
properties.ruleText: If an obstacle is detected in the picker’s current path (Obstacle Detection = True), then robotic picker immediately stops and recalculates a new path around the obstacle
properties.ruleHTML: If an obstacle is detected in the picker’s current path (Obstacle Detection = True), then robotic picker immediately stops and recalculates a new path around the obstacle

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.1.1.1
properties.ruleText: If no alternative path is available, proceed to the manual override request
properties.ruleHTML: If no alternative path is available, proceed to the manual override request

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.2
properties.ruleText: robotic picker pause and retry after a short delay
properties.ruleHTML: robotic picker pause and retry after a short delay

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.2.1
properties.ruleText: If a temporary obstacle is detected and marked as temporary by the system, then robotic picker pauses and retries after a predefined delay (e.g., 10 seconds).
properties.ruleHTML: If a temporary obstacle is detected and marked as temporary by the system, then robotic picker pauses and retries after a predefined delay (e.g., 10 seconds).

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.2.1.1
properties.ruleText: If the obstacle persists after three retries, escalate to a recalculation of the path or manual intervention
properties.ruleHTML: If the obstacle persists after three retries, escalate to a recalculation of the path or manual intervention

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.3
properties.ruleText: robotic picker avoid collision with static objects
properties.ruleHTML: robotic picker avoid collision with static objects

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.3.1
properties.ruleText: If a static object is detected (e.g., pallet, shelf), then the robotic picker recalculates the route to avoid the static object.
properties.ruleHTML: If a static object is detected (e.g., pallet, shelf), then the robotic picker recalculates the route to avoid the static object.

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.3.1.1
properties.ruleText: If recalculation is not possible, alert the system for manual intervention
properties.ruleHTML: If recalculation is not possible, alert the system for manual intervention

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.4
properties.ruleText: robotic picker resumes normal operations
properties.ruleHTML: robotic picker resumes normal operations

properties.name: Robotic Picker - Object Detection in Pathfinding Algorithm.4.1
properties.ruleText: If no obstacle is detected (Obstacle Detection = False), then the robotic picker proceeds along the original or recalculated path to complete its assigned task
properties.ruleHTML: If no obstacle is detected (Obstacle Detection = False), then the robotic picker proceeds along the original or recalculated path to complete its assigned task

properties.name: Bill of lading
properties.documentation: A legal document issued by a carrier or its agent to the shipper acknowledges receipt of the goods and outlines the transportation agreement's terms. It serves as a receipt for the goods, evidence of the contract of carriage, and a document of title.

properties.name: Air Waybill
properties.documentation: A document used for the transportation of goods by air. It serves as a contract of carriage between the shipper and the carrier and includes details such as the origin and destination of the goods, the consignee, the nature of the goods, and the charges.

properties.name: Consignment Note
properties.documentation: A document used for the transportation of goods by road or rail. It includes details such as the name and address of the consignor and consignee, the nature of the goods, the quantity, the weight, and the mode of transport.

properties.name: Commercial Invoice
properties.documentation: A document that lists the goods being shipped, the price, and other details required for customs purposes. It is used to determine the value of the goods for customs duty and tax purposes.

properties.name: Packing List
properties.documentation: A document that details the contents of each package or container being shipped. It includes information such as each item's quantity, weight, and dimensions.

properties.name: Export Declaration
properties.documentation: A document required by customs authorities in some countries that provides information about the goods being exported, including their value, quantity, and destination.

properties.name: Insurance Certificate
properties.documentation: A document that serves as proof of insurance coverage for the goods being shipped.

properties.name: Shipment manifest
properties.documentation: A document that summarizes all the items included in a shipment. It typically includes information such as the total number of items, their weight, dimensions, and value, as well as the name and address of the shipper, the carrier, and the consignee. A shipment manifest is used by carriers to keep track of the items in a shipment, and it may also be used by customs officials to verify the shipment's contents.

properties.name: Bill of exchange
properties.documentation: A financial document used in international trade to facilitate the payment of goods or services. It is a written order from the exporter (seller) to the importer (buyer) to pay a specific amount on a certain date or demand. The exporter sends the bill of exchange to the importer, who then accepts it by signing it and acknowledging the amount due and the payment terms. The bill of exchange is an essential financial document used in international trade that provides security and flexibility for both the exporter and importer.

properties.name: Advance Cargo Information (ACI)
properties.documentation: Information that ensures efficient cargo movement across borders while complying with customs regulations and requirements.

properties.name: Shipment
properties.documentation:
A Shipment is the process of transporting orders from the warehouse to customers. Shipments have attributes like a unique identifier (ShipmentID), order ID, shipment date, carrier, and tracking number. They are critical for tracking the delivery status of orders and ensuring timely fulfillment.

This includes details about the shipment, such as the bill of lading number, booking number, container number, flight number, or vessel name.
properties.examples:
• Shipment ID
  • Transportation Order ID (foreign key)
  • Carrier ID (foreign key)
  • Mode of Transport (e.g., Truck, Air, Rail, Ocean)
  • Shipment Date
  • Estimated Arrival Date
  • Actual Arrival Date
  • Tracking Number
  • Current Status (e.g., Dispatched, In-Transit, Delivered, Exception)

properties.name: Cargo Information
properties.documentation: This includes a cargo description, such as the type of goods, weight, quantity, and value.

properties.name: Consignee Information
properties.documentation: This includes the name and address of the person or entity receiving the cargo.

properties.name: Notify Party Information
properties.documentation: This includes the name and address of the party that should be notified when the cargo arrives.

properties.name: Port of Loading Information
properties.documentation: This includes the name and location of the port where the cargo is being loaded.

properties.name: Port of Discharge Information
properties.documentation: This includes the name and location of the port where the cargo will be unloaded.

properties.name: Country of Origin Information
properties.documentation: This includes the country where the cargo was produced or manufactured.

properties.name: Harmonized System (HS) Code
properties.documentation: This standardized code is used to classify goods for customs purposes. The Harmonized System is a standardized numerical method of classifying traded products. It is used by customs authorities worldwide to identify products when assessing duties and taxes and for gathering statistics. The HS is administrated by the World Customs Organization (WCO) and is updated every five years.

properties.name: Carrier Information
properties.documentation: This includes the name and address of the carrier responsible for transporting the cargo.

properties.name: Freight Information
properties.documentation: This includes details about the cargo's cost, such as the freight rate and any surcharges.

properties.name: Shipper
properties.documentation: This includes the shipper's name, address, and contact details (the party sending the goods).

properties.name: Shipment terms
properties.documentation: The terms and conditions of the transportation agreement between the shipper and the carrier. This may include details about liability, insurance, freight charges, and any special instructions or requirements.

properties.name: Destination
properties.documentation: The final destination where the goods are delivered.

properties.name: Description of Goods
properties.documentation: A detailed description of the goods being transported. This includes quantity, weight, dimensions, packaging type, and any special handling instructions.

properties.name: Origin
properties.documentation: The place where the shipment originates (origin).

properties.name: Date and Signatures
properties.documentation: The date when the bill of lading is issued, along with signatures or stamps from the carrier or its agent, acknowledging receipt of the goods in the stated condition.

properties.name: Transportation Service
properties.documentation: A service provided by carriers or logistics companies to move goods or passengers from one location to another.

properties.name: Carrier
properties.documentation: Responsible for ensuring the safe, timely, and cost-effective movement of goods.
properties.examples:
• Carrier ID
  • Carrier Name
  • Carrier Type (e.g., Trucking, Air, Rail, Ocean)
  • Contact Information
  • Fleet Size
  • Service Area
  • Pricing Model (Rate per Mile, Flat Rate, etc.)
  • Performance Metrics (e.g., On-time Delivery Rate)

properties.name: Certificate of Origin
properties.documentation: A document that certifies the country where the goods originated. It may be required by customs authorities to determine tariffs and trade restrictions based on the origin of the goods.

properties.name: Customs Declaration/Custom Forms
properties.documentation: Forms are required by customs authorities and contain information about the contents of the shipment, its value, origin, destination, and other details necessary for customs clearance.

properties.name: Dangerous Goods Declaration
properties.documentation: A document is required for shipments containing hazardous materials. It provides information about the nature, quantity, and handling instructions for the dangerous goods being transported, ensuring compliance with regulations.

properties.name: Purchase Order
properties.documentation: A document is issued by a buyer to a seller, specifying the goods or services being ordered, quantities, prices, and transaction terms.

properties.name: Warehouse Receipt
properties.documentation: Issued by a warehouse upon receiving goods, this document serves as proof of receipt and may include details such as the condition of the goods, quantities, and other relevant information.

properties.name: Inventory Report
properties.documentation: This document provides a comprehensive overview of current inventory levels, including stock quantities, locations, and other inventory-related details.

properties.name: Shipping Labels
properties.documentation: Labels affixed to packages or containers containing information such as the destination address, handling instructions, barcode, and other identifiers for tracking and sorting during transportation.

properties.name: Delivery Note
properties.documentation: A document accompanying a shipment that lists the contents of the delivery. It may include details like item descriptions, quantities, and any discrepancies found at the time of delivery.

properties.name: Material Safety Data Sheet
properties.documentation: An essential document for hazardous materials, an MSDS provides detailed information about the properties, handling, storage, and safety precautions for substances or products.

properties.name: Transportation Management System Documents
properties.documentation: These documents encompass items managed within a TMS, such as carrier contracts, rate agreements, transportation plans, and routing instructions.

properties.name: Proof of Delivery
properties.documentation: A document acknowledging the successful delivery of goods, signed by the recipient or receiver. It confirms receipt and completion of the delivery process.

properties.name: Return Merchandise Authorization
properties.documentation: A document authorizing the return of goods, specifying reasons for return, conditions, and instructions for the return process.
properties.examples:
• RMA ID,
  • Customer ID,
  • Order ID,
  • Product ID,
  • Return Reason,
  • Return Date,
  • RMA Status (e.g., Pending, Approved, Rejected),
  • Inspection Report,
  • Action Taken (e.g., Restock, Repair, Recycle, Dispose).

properties.name: Logistics Service Provider (LSP) Agreements
properties.documentation: Contracts and agreements between companies and logistics service providers, outlining services, terms, and conditions for transportation, warehousing, or other logistics-related activities.

properties.name: Picking List
properties.documentation: A list of items that need to be picked for the order.

extensionElements.content: Usage: Guides the warehouse staff on what items to pick.

properties.name: Compliance Checklist
properties.documentation: A checklist of air transport regulations and requirements.

extensionElements.content: Usage: Ensures items meet air transport compliance before packaging.

properties.examples: Attributes: Compliance criteria, inspection status, notes on any issues.

properties.name: Pallet Information
properties.documentation: Details about the pallet used for storing the items.

extensionElements.content: Helps in identifying and managing the pallet during the process.

properties.examples: Attributes: Pallet ID, contents, weight, dimensions.

properties.name: Packaging Instructions
properties.documentation: Instructions for selecting appropriate packaging materials based on item characteristics.

extensionElements.content: Ensures the correct packaging is used for air transport.

properties.examples: Attributes: Item ID, recommended packaging materials, special handling instructions.

properties.name: Air Transport Labels
properties.documentation: Labels required for air transport, including special handling labels.

extensionElements.content: Usage: Ensures packages are properly labeled according to air transport regulations.

properties.examples: Attributes: Label type, item ID, handling instructions.

properties.name: Final Inspection Report
properties.documentation: Report generated after the final inspection before dispatch.

extensionElements.content: Confirms that all items and packages meet quality and compliance standards.

properties.examples: Attributes: Inspection criteria, status, inspector ID, notes on any issues.

properties.name: Loading Area Schedule
properties.documentation: Schedule and details for moving packages to the loading area.

extensionElements.content: Usage: Ensures timely and organized movement of packages to the loading area.

properties.examples: Attributes: Loading area ID, time slot, package IDs, handler ID.

properties.name: Destination Control Statement
properties.documentation: This statement verifies that the items are being shipped in accordance with the laws of the destination country. It includes information such as the product, country of origin, country of destination, estimated value, and the shipper's name and address. The destination control statement often appears on commercial invoices, airway bills of lading, and shipper's export declarations (SEDs)

properties.name: Air Transport Documentation
properties.documentation: Includes all necessary documents for air transport.

extensionElements.content: Air waybill, customs declarations, packing list, compliance certificates.

properties.examples: Air waybill, customs declarations, packing list, compliance certificates.

properties.name: Loading Instruction Form (LIF)
properties.documentation: Specification of the hold compartment loading is usually achieved by the completion of a Loading Instruction Form (LIF).

properties.name: Order
properties.documentation: An Order is a request for products made by a customer. Each order has attributes like a unique identifier (Order ID), order date, customer name, and total amount. Orders detail the products requested by customers and are essential for tracking sales and fulfillment.

properties.name: Warehouse
properties.documentation: A Warehouse is a physical location where products are stored. It has attributes such as a unique identifier (WarehouseID), name, location, and capacity. The warehouse plays a crucial role in housing inventory and facilitating the management of stock levels, shipping, and receiving goods.

properties.name: Product
properties.documentation: A Product is an item stored in the warehouse, ready to be sold or shipped. Each product has attributes like a unique identifier (ProductID), name, description, category, price, and weight. Products can be classified into different types such as perishable, non-perishable, or fragile.

properties.name: Employee
properties.documentation: An Employee is a person who works at the warehouse. Employees have attributes such as a unique identifier (EmployeeID), name, position, and hire date. Employees can have different roles, including managers, warehouse workers, and administrative staff, each contributing to the smooth operation of the warehouse.

properties.name: Inventory
properties.documentation: Inventory represents the stock of products available in the warehouse. It includes attributes such as a unique identifier (InventoryID), warehouse ID, product ID, quantity, and reorder level. Inventory management ensures that the right amount of product is available to meet demand without overstocking.

properties.name: Location
properties.documentation: The Location entity represents the geographical and physical address information associated with various components of the Warehouse Management System, such as warehouses, employees, and orders. This entity is crucial for identifying and managing the physical places where activities occur, ensuring that logistics and operations are well-coordinated.

Customers have both billing and shipping addresses to manage payment and delivery logistics.

  • Billing Address: Location 1

  • Preferred Carrier

properties.name: Cost Data
properties.documentation: Data on holding costs, ordering costs, and shortage costs.

properties.name: Supplier
properties.documentation: A Supplier is an external entity that provides products to the warehouse. Suppliers have attributes such as a unique identifier (SupplierID), name, contact information, and address. They are essential for maintaining the inventory levels by supplying necessary goods. It also contains information on lead times and delivery performance.

properties.name: Inventory Manager
properties.documentation: Inventory managers work in various settings across different industries, reflecting the broad applicability of their skills. In warehouses, distribution and fulfillment centers, they handle large volumes of products, manage storage, and coordinate shipping to various locations.
properties.examples: Third-party logistics providers (3PLs), wholesale distributors, and e-commerce fulfillment centers.

properties.name: Stowage Plan
properties.documentation: A storage plan is a layout for cargo transport to optimize the placement and arrangement of items or goods within a storage space.

extensionElements.content:
The primary objectives of a stowage plan are to:

  1. Maximize Space Utilization: Efficiently use available storage space to accommodate as many items as possible.
  2. Ensure Safe Handling: Arrange items in a way that prevents damage during storage or transport.
  3. Facilitate Easy Access: Organize goods for quick retrieval, reducing the time needed for loading, unloading.
  4. Maintain Balance and Stability: In the case of transport, ensure that the load is evenly distributed to maintain stability and safety.
  5. Comply with Regulations: Adhere to legal or industry-specific guidelines, such as weight limits or hazardous material handling protocols.

properties.name: Transport Order
properties.documentation: A record is created to capture the details of a customer's shipment request, including the items to be shipped, origin and destination locations, and any other relevant shipping instructions.
properties.examples:
• Transport Order ID
  • Transport Order Date
  • Customer ID (foreign key)
  • Origin Location ID (foreign key)
  • Destination Location ID (foreign key)
  • Shipment ID (foreign key)
  • Order Status (e.g., Pending, In-Transit, Delivered, Cancelled)
  • Total Weight
  • Total Volume
  • Priority Level
  • Expected Delivery Date
  • Special Instructions

properties.name: Vehicle
properties.documentation: A mode of transport used by a carrier to move goods from one place to another. Vehicles can include trucks, vans, planes, ships, and other means of transportation.
properties.examples:
• Vehicle ID
  • Carrier ID (foreign key)
  • Vehicle Type (e.g., Truck, Van, Plane, Ship)

properties.name: Driver

properties.name: Route
properties.documentation: The path or course taken by a vehicle to move goods from the origin location to the destination location. Routes are optimized for efficiency, cost, and time.

properties.name: Rate
properties.documentation: The cost associated with transporting goods between two locations, provided by a carrier. Rates can vary based on distance, mode of transport, weight, and volume of the shipment.
properties.examples:

properties.name: Invoice
properties.documentation: A document issued by the carrier or transportation service provider to the customer, detailing the services provided, costs incurred, and payment terms for the transportation order.

• Invoice ID

  • Invoice Date
  • Due Date

properties.name: Contract

properties.examples:
• Contract ID
  • Carrier ID (foreign key)
  • Customer ID (foreign key)
  • Start Date
  • End Date
  • Terms and Conditions
  • Agreed Rates
  • Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

properties.name: Unit Cost

properties.name: Truckload Lot

properties.name: Truckload Carriers

properties.name: Truck Stop Electrification

properties.name: Trend Forecasting Models

properties.name: Transportation Planning Systems
properties.documentation: Software or tools are used for planning, optimizing, and managing the transportation of goods to ensure efficient routes, cost-effectiveness, and timely delivery.

properties.name: Transportation Mode
properties.documentation: The method or means by which goods or passengers are transported, for example, by air, rail, road, or sea.

properties.name: Manufacture recall notice
properties.examples:
Attributes:

  1. Recall Notice ID: Unique identifier for the recall notice (e.g., UUID or serial number).
  2. Manufacturer Name: The name of the manufacturer issuing the recall.
  3. Recall Date: The date when the recall notice was issued.
  4. Product Name: The name of the product being recalled.
  5. Product ID: The unique identifier or model number of the recalled product.
  6. Reason for Recall: A brief description of the reason for the recall (e.g., safety issue, defect, non-compliance).
  7. Affected Batches: Batch numbers or ranges of serial numbers affected by the recall.
  8. Recall Severity: Classification of the recall’s severity (e.g., Class I, Class II, Class III).
  9. Corrective Action: Instructions provided by the manufacturer on what should be done with the recalled product (e.g., return, repair, refund).
  10. Contact Information: Details on how customers or distributors can contact the manufacturer for further information.
  11. Distribution Channels: Channels through which the recalled product was distributed (e.g., retail, wholesale, direct-to-consumer).
  12. Regulatory Agency: The name of the regulatory agency overseeing the recall, if applicable (e.g., FDA, CPSC).
  13. Status: Current status of the recall (e.g., active, resolved, pending).
  14. Notification Method: How the recall notice was communicated (e.g., email, mail, press release).

properties.name: Repair Facility
properties.examples: Attributes: Facility ID, Location, Repair Capacity, Repair Time Estimates, Cost of Repair.

properties.text:
Process Flow:
Customer Initiates Return:

The customer contacts customer service to request an RMA.
The system generates an RMA ID linked to the customer's order and product details.
Product Return & Receiving:

The product is shipped back to the warehouse.
Upon receipt, the warehouse updates the inventory and the RMA status.
Product Inspection:

The product undergoes inspection to assess its condition.
The inspection report determines whether the product can be restocked, repaired, recycled, or disposed of.
Action Decision:

Based on the inspection, the system updates the RMA with the action taken.
If repair is needed, the product is sent to a repair facility.
If the product is to be recycled or disposed of, it is sent to the appropriate facility.
Final Outcome:

If the product is restocked, inventory levels are updated.
If the product is recycled or disposed of, environmental reports are generated.
The RMA is closed once the final action is completed, and the customer is notified of the outcome.
